name: Stefano Ricci
why: Silk ties, shirts and clothing in an opulent Florentine style.
origin: Founded in Florence in 1972 by Stefano Ricci.

notes.boat: The same register as Zilli, in Florence, and equally unbothered about the distinction between a yacht and a stage.
notes.ital: Florence, with its own silk mill at Antico Setificio Fiorentino. Maximal Italian luxury, unembarrassed about it, and vertically integrated further than most houses three times its size.

notes.craft: Stefano Ricci states a 9,000 m2 production base in Fiesole and owns the Antico Setificio Fiorentino silk mill. Every sampled PDP says Made in Italy. The site does not show which categories the Fiesole site actually makes, though, and tie printing is done with Como partners. Real owned making, coverage of the range unshown: 4.

craft_evidence.owned_d: One Family Story page: production headquartered in Fiesole near Florence, 'more than 9,000 square metres', with an all-Italian workforce of 900. Owns the Antico Setificio Fiorentino (silk mill operating since 1786, acquired 2010) and, since 2025, Moleria Locchi (crystal workshop). The Crafting the Arts page describes in-house Florentine tailors, leather, jewellery and silver work; tie silk is printed with Como suppliers.
